hydro_engineer.text: Four turbines, fed by a headrace canal from the Shannon and dropping the water about thirty metres. When it opened in 1929 it was the biggest hydro station in the world.
The Shannon Scheme was the Free State's big bet: the whole country wired up from one river. It worked. Your granny's first light bulb probably came from here.

hydro_eel.text: The eels still try to get up the river past the dam. We catch them below and carry them up in tanks. Trap and transport, they call it. I call it eel taxi.
